### Requirements and solution

Carry the four goals and the source's canonical-consistency boundary together:
agents may choose suitable means inside agreed scope and protections, but must
demonstrate the result. Canonical policies, contracts and authorized decisions
must agree for the same scope/version. Clear precedence permits an in-scope
correction of a stale subordinate statement; genuine authority conflicts stop
affected consumption for owner reconciliation, not silent selection.

Integrate a small outcome-and-boundary contract into existing authorities.
Distinguish mandatory controls from adaptable defaults/examples. Reuse valid
authorization while preserving actual new acceptance boundaries. Do not add
an exhaustive rulebook or arbitrary file/snapshot-volume gate.

For review evidence, prefer retained immutable Git base/candidate commits and
concise findings, resolutions, decisions and meaningful validation. Preserve
retrievable exact bytes: a hash is not a recovery source. Keep necessary unique
raw/non-Git material and local snapshots consumed by the current checker.
Do not prune historical evidence under this delivery's implementation scope.

### Contracts to formalize and source mapping

C01–C06 and their source links remain canonical in the accepted whiteboard:
quality-policy consistency/precedence; skill/generator action boundaries;
scoped batch versus ordinary routes; minimum review evidence; checker-required
snapshot exceptions; and consumer/README/example consistency. The plan should
map these to observable acceptance cases, not copy the whole source discussion.

### Delivery boundaries and required evidence

One self-contained T01 may target main through its reviewed PR after approved
planning and readiness. Its source boundary is the whiteboard's enumerated
policy/docs/skills/template/example/test set, plus generated guidance only in
install-sdd.sh. Use the policy's complete plan because the change is systemic.
No task, PR or implementation mode is selected by this handoff.

Preserve schema fields/states, quorum, approval invalidation, retry limits,
retention deadlines and merge controls. If implementation needs one of these
changed, return with an explicit design amendment. Preserve old installed pins
and historical bytes; compatibility notes explain adoption. Rollback is a
reviewed coherent revert, not deletion of review history.

Validate representative cases for canonical conflict versus stale summary,
retained approval, bounded reversible recovery, changed scope and uncertain
destruction; Git multi-round review, missing evidence, unique raw material and
checker snapshots. Run relevant positive/negative tests and complete project
documentation/regression checks; verify generated guides/installed skill links
where changed. Semantic reviewers reconcile complete impacted sources and
README/diagrams. Syntax passes alone do not prove consistency or saved effort.

Runtime #33/#34/#36 and U84 remain deferred to the repository owner. No new
owner preference remains in the accepted design. Actual scenario results,
implementation and performance evidence remain unproduced.
